Agent sessions

agentd runs coding agents as Bus sessions. Anything on the Bus can start one: Workshop, a terminal, a Mix script, or another agent. Each running agent's output is published as Bus events, so any number of watchers can follow a turn. When the agent asks permission to do something, the question goes to the human on the desk they are looking at, through notifyd.

agentd speaks the Agent Client Protocol (ACP) to the agent. ACP is the open standard that most coding agents already support, so one integration covers them all. agentd adds what ACP lacks: addressing across the mesh, many watchers, and a human in the loop. Every session also gets mixos-mcp, so the agent can use the Bus in turn. The rules are in the decision.

 Bus callers ── agent.* commands, agent.session.* topics ──► agentd
                                                              │ ACP over the agent's stdio
                                                              ▼
                                                     agent (claude-agent-acp, …)
                                                              │ MCP
                                                              ▼
                                                 mixos-mcp ──► back onto the Bus

Run it as a session service: mix --serve agentd.mix --name agent. It needs a mix with process_watch stdin pipes (stdin: "pipe", process_write). Two units ship with it:

  • agentd.service, a user unit (systemctl --user enable --now) for a user's own session, always running. The user cannot write <etc> or <var>, so it reads ~/.config/mixos/agent.conf.mix and keeps the log in ~/.local/state/mixos/agentd/. With no conf file the unit is skipped.
  • agentd@.service, for console desk session %i, run as the desk user.

Configuration

agentd reads $MIXOS_AGENTD_CONF, else <etc>/agent.conf.mix. The file is strict data:

max_live: 4
agents: {
  claude: {argv: ["claude-agent-acp"], roots: ["/home/user/src"]},
  gemini: {argv: ["gemini", "--acp", "--skip-trust"], roots: ["/home/user/src"]},
  opencode: {argv: ["opencode", "acp"], roots: ["/home/user/src"], policy: "ask"}
}

Tested agents (2026-10-30), each with mixos-mcp reaching the Bus:

AgentargvNotes
Claudeclaude-agent-acp (npm @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp)Uses its own file and shell tools, so Claude Code hooks such as a PreToolUse gate still apply.
Gemini CLIgemini --acp --skip-trustWithout --skip-trust Gemini treats the folder as untrusted and starts no MCP server. The flag trusts the session's cwd for that run only, so roots should hold only trusted code. Reads go through fs/read_text_file. Its write tool cannot create a new file through any ACP client: it checks for a missing file with instanceof Error, which a JSON-RPC error is not, so it falls back to its own shell.
Codexcodex-acp (npm @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp)Uses the normal Codex login and CODEX_HOME. It starts MCP servers with a bare environment, so agentd passes its own broker and layout variables (MIXOS_NODED_URL, MIXOS_BUS_SOCKET, MIXOS_RUN, …) in the mixos-mcp entry.
OpenCodeopencode acpThe model is a config option: agent.session.set {session, option: "model", value: "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro"}.

  • argv: the agent's ACP command, run directly (no shell).

  • roots: the directories a session's cwd and additional_dirs must lie under. Paths are resolved first, so a symlink cannot escape. This confines only what the agent asks agentd for. The agent's own tools, such as a shell, are not sandboxed by agentd.

  • policy:

    • ask (the default) sends every permission request to the human.
    • allow_once lets agentd answer allow_once by itself.

    agentd never answers allow_always.

  • permission_timeout_s (default 300): with no answer by then, the request is rejected. No answer is never yes.

  • max_live (default 4): live sessions at once. It is a hard cap, and agent-started sessions count against it.

  • log_keep_days (default 30): how long the session log keeps a session after it ends.

Commands

Bodies are JSON objects.

CommandBodyReply
agent.agentsthe configured agents, live count and cap
agent.session.new{agent, cwd, mode?, additional_dirs?}{session, status} at once; ready follows as an event
agent.session.prompt{session, content}{session, turn}; the turn streams as events
agent.session.cancel{session}cancels the running turn
agent.session.close{session}ends the agent (stdin closes; an agent still running 10 s later is stopped); the session stays in the log and can be resumed
agent.session.resume{session}{session, status, via} at once: brings back an ended session (see Resuming)
agent.session.set{session, mode} or {session, option, value}sets a mode, or a config option such as the model
agent.session.listlive and recently ended sessions
agent.session.read{session, since?, limit?}the session and its logged events after seq: {session, events, more, next}
agent.permission.respond{session, request, option}answers a permission request

content is a string, or a list of ACP content blocks.

A read returns at most limit events (default and maximum 2000) and about 32 MiB. When more is true, read again with since set to next.

The acting commands (new, prompt, cancel, close, set, respond) take an optional id of 1-128 characters from [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. Ids are scoped to the session (to new for agent.session.new). A retry with the same id gets the first reply and never runs again, so a caller that lost a reply can safely send the command again. If agentd stopped after logging a command but before replying, the retry gets COMMAND_INTERRUPTED; the command is not run again.

Refusals carry {error_code, message}:

rcerror_code
10USAGE, OUTSIDE_ROOTS or UNKNOWN_AGENT
14UNKNOWN_SESSION
15AGENT_RUNNING (a turn is already running), AGENT_NOT_READY, COMMAND_INTERRUPTED or AGENT_NOT_RESUMABLE
16AGENT_LIMIT or AGENT_DEPTH
17AGENT_SELF

Events

TopicBody
agent.session.updated{session, seq, kind, …}
agent.session.ended{session, exit_code, signal}
agent.permission.requested{session, request, title, options}

kind on agent.session.updated is one of:

  • initialized or ready;
  • an ACP update kind (agent_message_chunk, tool_call, plan, …), with the update unchanged in update;
  • stop, with stop set to end_turn, max_tokens, max_turn_requests, refusal or cancelled;
  • permission_answered;
  • error;
  • fs_read, fs_write or fs_refused (see Files);
  • terminal_created or terminal_exited (see Terminals);
  • ended, logged (not published) when a restart ends a session;
  • resumed (with via, the agent's info and capabilities) or resume_failed (see Resuming).

seq rises by one per event in a session. A watcher that missed events reads them back with agent.session.read {since}.

Resuming

agent.session.resume {session} brings back a session that ended, whether it was closed, its agent exited, or agentd restarted. Nothing resumes by itself. The session keeps its id, its mcp-s-<session>- Bus name and its log, and seq carries on. agentd starts the agent again and asks it to reopen its own record of the session:

  • session/resume when the agent offered it at initialize (no replay);
  • otherwise session/load. The agent then replays the conversation, which the log already holds, so replayed messages, tool calls and plans are dropped; current state (mode, commands, config options) is kept.

The current configuration decides: the agent must still be configured and the session's directories must still lie under its roots. A resume counts against max_live, and like new it is refused to a session's own agent (AGENT_SELF) and to a child session (AGENT_DEPTH). An agent that offers neither method gets AGENT_NOT_RESUMABLE before anything starts. If the agent refuses (it no longer has the session) or exits first, the session goes back to ended exactly as it was, with a resume_failed event. Gemini CLI answers session/load first and replays after, so after a load the session stays starting (a prompt is queued) until the replay has been quiet for a second, and replayed history is dropped until then.

agentd does not restore the mode or model (set them again) or a permission question that was open when the session ended (prompt again). Advertised at initialize: Claude, OpenCode and Codex offer session/resume; Gemini offers session/load.

Command line

mix agent drives agentd from a shell or the Mix prompt. Each command is one Bus call, except send --wait, which follows the turn on the topics (it runs as a short-lived Bus citizen, so nothing polls) and streams the agent's text.

CommandDoes
mix agent agentsthe configured agents
mix agent listlive and recent sessions
mix agent start AGENT [--cwd DIR] [--dir DIR]... [--mode M] [--id ID]starts a session; prints its id (cwd defaults to the current directory)
mix agent send SESSION TEXT... [--wait] [--timeout S] [--id ID]sends a prompt; with --wait, streams the turn and exits with its outcome
mix agent read SESSION [--since N] [--json]the session's events, one per line
mix agent answer SESSION REQUEST OPTIONanswers a permission question
mix agent cancel|close|resume SESSION [--id ID]as the Bus commands
mix agent set SESSION --mode M or --option NAME --value Vsets a mode or a config option

Exit codes: 0 done (end_turn), 1 refused, failed, or a turn that stopped another way, 2 the turn is waiting on a human (a permission question: answer it, then send or read again), 64 usage, 124 --wait timed out (the turn goes on). Exit 2 means a question is still open: one an allow_once policy answers at once does not stop --wait. --id makes a retried command safe: agentd runs it once and replays its first answer.

Session log

agentd writes every event and every acting command to a SQLite log before it publishes the event or runs the command: $MIXOS_AGENTD_DB, else <var>/agentd/sessions.db. The log outlives agentd. After a restart:

  • ended sessions and their events can still be listed and read;
  • command receipts still answer retries;
  • the agents that were running are gone (agentd owned them), so their sessions are ended with a last ended event whose reason is agentd_restart.

Sessions are dropped from the log log_keep_days after they end.

If the log cannot be written (a full disk), commands are refused, but the agent's events are still published and the gap is reported on stderr. A watcher that follows seq should therefore also check the session's status in a read: after such a gap and a restart, the ended event can carry a seq the watcher has already seen.

Files

agentd serves ACP's fs/read_text_file (with line and limit) and fs/write_text_file, inside the session's cwd and additional_dirs only. Paths must be absolute and are resolved first, so a symlink or .. cannot lead out; a new file's parent directory must already exist. A read is limited to 8 MiB. Refusals are JSON-RPC errors: -32002 for a missing file, -32602 for a path outside the session or a bad request. Every read, write and refusal is an event (fs_read, fs_write, fs_refused).

This confines what the agent asks agentd to do. An agent's own tools, such as its shell or Claude's built-in file tools, do not go through agentd. The path check and the read or write are separate steps, so an agent that replaces a path with a symlink between them can still lead one out; that takes the agent's own tools, which reach the same files anyway. A missing path outside the session is answered as outside, so the errors do not tell the agent what exists elsewhere.

Terminals

agentd serves ACP's terminal/* on the headless path: the command runs directly on pipes (no shell, no PTY), in the session's cwd or a cwd inside its directories, with the instance env plus any the agent asks for. agentd keeps the newest 5,000 lines of stdout and stderr together, up to outputByteLimit bytes (at most 8 MiB), dropping from the front. Terminal query sequences (cursor and device status requests, colour queries) are removed, since nothing is there to answer them. A session has at most 8 terminals at once, and they end with it. terminal/kill stops the command (TERM, then KILL) and reports SIGTERM, even when KILL was needed. Each terminal's start and exit are events (terminal_created, terminal_exited).

On a desk, terminals are to move onto Term, so a human can watch them.

Agents calling back

agentd runs every agent with MIXOS_AGENT_SESSION set to its session id, and that agent's mixos-mcp registers on the Bus as mcp-s-<session>-<suffix>. The broker stamps that name as the sender of everything the bridge sends, so agentd recognises a session's own agent:

  • It cannot act on its own session (AGENT_SELF): no answering its own permission requests, no prompting or closing itself.
  • A session it starts is a child, and a child cannot start sessions (AGENT_DEPTH).
  • The max_live cap holds for everyone.

This catches the agent's MCP path. An agent with a shell can still open a Bus client of its own, which is why the cap and the human answer matter.
